subject: [PATCH 2/2] sched/numa: scan read-only file mappings in tiering mode

reviews.author: Gregory Price
reviews.summary: Addressed some concerns regarding unneeded rescanning, but acknowledged that there are still issues with concurrent scanners and ptl lock contention. Plans to push a v2 after additional testing.
reviews.raw_body:
On Fri, Sep 04, 2026 at 02:20:06PM -0400, Gregory Price wrote:
> @@ -4302,7 +4316,7 @@ static void task_numa_work(struct callback_head *work)
>  		 * VMA can cause others to become "permanently unaccessed" if a scan
>  		 * cycle is consumed entirely by the large VMA.
>  		 */
> -		vma->numab_state->slow_only = false;
> +		vma->numab_state->slow_only = ro_file;
>  		if (!vma_pids_forced && !vma_is_accessed(mm, vma)) {
>  			if (!(sysctl_numa_balancing_mode &
>  			      NUMA_BALANCING_MEMORY_TIERING)) {

Sashiko thinks this causes unneeded rescanning, but I don't think it
does. The cursor prevents it from restarting, and when we loop back
around reset_ptenuma_scan() bumps the sequence.

It also had concerns about concurrent scanners and ptl lock contention,
but mm->numa_next_scan only admits one per scan period.

Either way on a rewalk the scan hits pte_protnone() and moves on.

~Gregory

2026-09-04.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a memory tiering issue where read-only file-backed mappings are not being scanned in tiering mode, leading to inefficient page placement and unneeded rescanning. The patch introduces a new function `vma_is_ro_file` to identify such mappings and modifies the `task_numa_work` function to scan these VMAs with the slow_only restriction. This change ensures that only non-toptier folios are made hint-faultable, preventing unnecessary promotion of pages.
